title: Training-free Truthfulness Detection via Sparse MLP Value Vectors

problem.claim: Large language models can generate factually incorrect content, creating a need to assess truthfulness from internal model signals.

gap.claim: Existing supervised probing requires labeled data and classifier training, while training-free methods use coarse activation statistics that provide limited insight into the origin of truthfulness-related signals.

contributions.claim: A training-free truthfulness-detection approach operates on individual MLP value vectors.
TruthV aggregates preferences expressed by relevant MLP value vectors during inference.
The approach identifies a sparse subset of value vectors with stable, directionally consistent correlations with content truthfulness.

author_reported_evidence.claim: TruthV requires only a small support set and adds no model parameters or classifier weights.
TruthV was evaluated across model scales from 2B to 13B and across question answering, natural language understanding, and hallucination benchmarks.
TruthV consistently outperformed existing training-free baselines.

narrative_sequence.summary: LLMs generate factually incorrect content, motivating truthfulness assessment from internal signals.
Supervised and existing training-free approaches have data, training, or interpretability limitations.
The work analyzes individual MLP value vectors and proposes TruthV to aggregate their preferences.
TruthV is evaluated across model scales and several benchmark categories.
The authors report consistent improvement over training-free baselines and sparse, structured truthfulness-related variation in MLP value vectors.

source_observation.claim: Only a sparse subset of MLP value vectors shows stable and directionally consistent truthfulness correlations.

interpretation.claim: Truthfulness-related internal signals may be concentrated in a small, structured subset of model components.

application.claim: For similar inference tasks, inspect and aggregate signals from selectively identified internal components rather than relying only on global activation statistics.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether this sparse-component strategy transfers beyond the evaluated model scales, benchmarks, or truthfulness tasks.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the support-set construction procedure.
The abstract does not report quantitative performance gains or benchmark results.
The abstract does not describe which models or datasets were used beyond the stated scales and benchmark categories.
